headline: Language diversity sets Ward 14 apart, though housing investment lags far behind.
summary:
About eighty-five percent of Ward 14 residents use a language other than English inside the home, the highest rate of the fifty wards. That share comes from a ward stuck at 41st of 50 overall, deep in the bottom fifth of the rankings. Ward 14 covers Archer Heights, Gage Park, Chicago Lawn and Brighton Park on the Southwest Side. It also has the second-lowest share of people living alone, so more households here share a home than in nearly every other ward, and a modeled estimate puts it among the more religious wards, with the share of residents expected to report no religious affiliation running lower than in nearly all fifty. Median rent for renters paying cash rent is the third-lowest in the city, and ozone pollution is lower here than in all but four other wards.

The weak spots are investment and a handful of less common measures. Ward 14 sits last of the fifty on residential renovation permits issued, and last on the dollar value of recorded property sales in the latest year. It also carries the lowest density of massage and bodywork businesses in the city, and sits closer than anywhere else in Chicago to facilities that report toxic releases. Congregation counts trail the same way, with the fewest religious congregations carrying paid staff per resident anywhere in the fifty. Together, these numbers describe a linguistically diverse, family-dense residential ward with comparatively low housing turnover and more exposure to industrial sites than most of Chicago.
reading_the_rankings: Two of these figures need a closer look. The top rank on language, roughly eighty-five percent of residents reporting a home language besides English, comes from a direct Census Bureau count rather than a model, though the total still gets divided by how much land each tract covers, not by how many households sit inside it, so homes near the edge of Ward 14 could actually be counted toward a different ward's tally. The second-place mark on modeled no-religious-affiliation share looks just as solid, since a low modeled share counts as a strong score on this measure, but the two numbers come from different places entirely. A national survey pushed down to ward level produced this estimate, not a headcount taken inside Ward 14, and the group that built it calls the number low confidence. The last-place rank on religious congregations rests on ZIP code data, and ZIP codes don't follow ward boundaries at all, so this number may really describe a differently drawn area than Ward 14 itself.

news.headline: Amazon To Begin Demolition Of Central Steel & Wire Plant In Gage Park
news.note: Demolition began on the former Central Steel & Wire plant site to make way for a 230,000-square-foot Amazon delivery station.

news.headline: Cyclist Hit By Driver In Gage Park Faces Long Road To Recovery — And 'Overwhelming' Medical Debt
news.note: A 22-year-old cyclist was seriously injured when a driver hit him on South Western Avenue, and his family started a fundraiser to cover medical costs.

news.headline: 'Moving Archer Forward' Initiative Aims To Bring 800 New Housing Units To Archer Avenue
news.note: The same planning initiative is tagged to Gage Park and Brighton Park, and would add housing, retail space and transit upgrades along the Archer Avenue corridor over the next 10 to 20 years.
